content: Reductive groups are being formalized in TauCeti. What do you mean by Shimura varieties? The analytic theory or the algebraic theory or the arithmetic theory?
There is also ongoing work on Hodge structures in Tau Ceti

@Kevin Buzzard I was talking about the algebraic and arithmetic theory (when you say analytic theory, do mean locally symmetric spaces?). Mainly the works of Deligne. But, I am also not sure if this is a bit aspirational at the moment - that is why I was thinking of starting with Hodge structures.

@Chris Birkbeck I had a quick look at the GitHub page you mentioned and noticed that work on Hodge structures hasn't started. So, do you know of it would possible to contribute to it (I have already done a little but over the last few week)?
Yeah by analytic I just meant making them as manifolds. I think that contributions to TauCeti are typically done by AI. CM abelian varieties is something else we have essentially nothing about.
PS there seems to be a ton of stuff on Hodge structures already, I think it must have started, e.g. https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge/Orthogonal.html

@Kevin Buzzard Oops. I seemed to have missed that (it's hard to check the GitHub pages on my phone :sweat_smile:).
I would actually be interested in a project on formalising CM abelian varieties - has someone already started working on it (in which case I could help)?
I'm guessing you're talking about CM abelian varieties in the context of Canonical models, right?
AFAIK nobody is working on CM abelian varieties (but IIRC mathlib has a proof that abelian varieties are abelian, which is at least a start).

Abhijit A J said:

Chris Birkbeck I had a quick look at the GitHub page you mentioned and noticed that work on Hodge structures hasn't started. So, do you know of it would possible to contribute to it (I have already done a little but over the last few week)?

Sorry I should have been clearer, what I sent was the roadmap of what being done in Tau Ceti, but its a bit harder to see whats already there without looking at Github (or asking an AI to check for you).

@Kevin Buzzard Thanks a lot! I wouldn't mind starting a project on that (I'll look into it next week - I'm on holiday right now). Could you tell me how I should go about announcing that, or should I do as part of some other project? Basically, I'm absolutely blank when it's comes to dealing with such things.
@Chris Birkbeck Ah, okay. Thanks a lot. I'm sorry if my questions are rather silly - I'm a new convert to lean looking for a fun project :sweat_smile:

The way to start is to make your own CMAbelianVarieties repo and write down a definition (which you should discuss with Lean experts) and then choose a random theorem e.g. that a CM ab var over a char 0 field has a model over a number field and try to prove it.
@Kevin Buzzard Thanks a lot.

@Kevin Buzzard Have abelian varieties been formalised at all? I don't know if it is my inability to search, but I couldn't find them on mathlib (Gemini also told me that it has not been formalised). Or is it maybe a separate project?

Oh, I just found this theorem isCommMonObj_of_isProper_of_geometricallyIntegral, which I believe is what you were probably referring to in an earlier message. But, I guess the words "Abelian Vareities" have not been used anywhere?
